title: Design System: TutorDesk Evidence Conservation Lab

display.purpose: Names the active source as the primary artifact.

title.purpose: Names ledger rows, panels, and evidence groups.

body.purpose: Carries source excerpts and sustained explanatory reading.

label.purpose: Classifies instruments, revisions, state, and provenance nodes.

shadows.name: raised-examination-plane
shadows.purpose: Separates an examination sheet or open review drawer from the lab bench.

shadows.name: selected-evidence-edge
shadows.purpose: Marks a selected source row without making it float.

motion.name: peel-reveal
motion.purpose: Reveals a claim's evidence path from the left edge like an examination film.

motion.name: layer-shift
motion.purpose: Moves interactive examination film with restrained physicality.

motion.name: drawer-slide
motion.purpose: Opens and closes the consolidated review drawer.

motion.name: scrim-fade
motion.purpose: Clarifies modal review state without competing with the drawer.

motion.name: provenance-popover
motion.purpose: Reveals the in-situ provenance popover at its originating badge without spatial travel.

components.name: Primary Approval Button
components.description: Confirms an explicit human approval or shows a selected learning instrument.

components.name: Secondary Instrument Button

components.name: Reject Button
components.description: Rejects a proposed learner-state mutation with a distinct caution treatment.
components.css: .ds-btn-reject { min-height: 34px; padding: 7px 11px; border: 1px solid var(--warning, #733421); border-radius: 0; background: var(--paper-strong, #fbfcfa); color: var(--warning, #733421); font-family: var(--label, 'Barlow Lab', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-reject:hover { background: var(--accession-wash, #f2ddd1); } .ds-btn-reject:active { background: var(--warning, #733421); color: #fff; } .ds-btn-reject:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #0b67a0); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Citation Trigger
components.description: Anchors exact citation or learner-state provenance directly to the supported source text.
components.css: .ds-citation { min-height: 30px; padding: 1px 6px 2px; border: 1px solid var(--verdigris-deep, #29564e); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--paper-strong, #fbfcfa); color: var(--verdigris-deep, #29564e); font-family: var(--label, 'Barlow Lab', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); font-size: .74rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .04em; cursor: pointer; } .ds-citation:hover, .ds-citation[aria-expanded='true'], .ds-citation:active { background: var(--verdigris-deep, #29564e); color: #fff; } .ds-citation:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #0b67a0); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Pending Status Stamp
components.description: Marks a proposal that still requires an explicit human decision.
components.css: .ds-status-pending { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 26px; padding: 2px 7px; border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: 0; background: var(--paper-strong, #fbfcfa); color: var(--accession, #93411f); font-family: var(--label, 'Barlow Lab', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); font-size: .72rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Source Record
components.description: Identifies a source revision in the vault while preserving active-source context.
components.css: .ds-source-record { width: 100%; padding: 9px 4px; border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line-soft, #cbcfc8); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #24302b); text-align: left; cursor: pointer; } .ds-source-record strong, .ds-source-record span { display: block; } .ds-source-record span { margin-top: 3px; color: var(--ink-muted, #58645e); font-size: .74rem; } .ds-source-record:hover, .ds-source-record[aria-current='true'] { background: var(--verdigris-wash, #d9e6e1); } .ds-source-record:active { box-shadow: inset 5px 0 0 var(--verdigris, #477c72); } .ds-source-record:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #0b67a0); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Session Record
components.description: Keeps active Source Claims and practice attempts visible as compact examination context.
components.css: .ds-session-record { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto auto 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 7px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line, #9da59e); border-radius: 0; background: var(--paper-strong, #fbfcfa); color: var(--ink, #24302b); } .ds-session-label, .ds-session-record strong, .ds-session-record span { font-family: var(--label, 'Barlow Lab', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); font-size: .73rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-session-label { color: var(--ink-muted, #58645e); } .ds-session-record strong { color: var(--verdigris-deep, #29564e); }

narrative.overview:
TutorDesk treats knowledge as material under examination. Mineral paper, graphite notation, oxidized-green evidence marks, accession-orange review layers, hairline rules, and tabular identifiers make the interface feel like a working conservation bench: exacting, quiet, and visibly accountable.

The active source is the artifact, not background for a chat stream. The Workspace expresses this through Reversible Layers: explanations, questions, provenance, and learner-state proposals sit over or beside the source as inspectable examination film. The system is dense without feeling compressed, and every consequential state change remains visibly subject to human approval.
keyCharacteristics: Archival labels, accession marks, and hairline measurement rules.
Mineral-white planes with graphite text and sparing chromatic state.
Exact provenance opened in situ from the citation or learner-state badge.
Square controls and layered review materials with explicit approval states.

rules.name: The Chromatic Evidence Rule
rules.body: Green means grounded, selected, or traceable; orange means pending human review; neither color is ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Visible Focus Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus uses the dedicated blue outline and must never be replaced by a subtle color shift.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Atkinson carries meaning; Barlow Condensed carries classification, state, and control.

rules.name: The Source Majority Rule
rules.body: In every workstation composition, the source remains the largest or first reading plane; capability controls orbit it rather than becoming a dominant chat rail.

rules.name: The Evidentiary Depth Rule
rules.body: A layer may rise only when its overlap communicates source, provenance, or approval state.

rules.name: The Capsule Exception Rule
rules.body: Only inline citation triggers use the capsule radius; actions, stamps, panels, and navigation remain square.

rules.name: The Immediate Provenance Rule
rules.body: The complete evidence chain opens where the citation is read; it never requires a spatial jump away from the source.

dos: Do make the source the primary visual artifact and open exact provenance in situ from its attached badge.
Do use accession labels, revision identifiers, and tabular numerals to make evidence feel inspectable.
Do keep the compact Session record limited to active Source Claims and practice attempts.
Do keep contextual approval controls beside the proposal and repeat every unresolved item in the consolidated queue.
Do support hover, click, keyboard focus, touch toggle, Escape/outside-click dismissal, focus return, reduced-motion disclosure, and 44px narrow-screen touch targets.
Do use material layers, hairlines, and tonal washes before reaching for shadow.
donts: Don't organize the workstation around a dominant chat rail.
Don't use gradients, glassy floating cards, soft rounded dashboards, or decorative color as substitutes for hierarchy.
Don't send provenance to a bottom strip, distant side panel, or secondary journey, and don't summarize away the exact citation path.
Don't use green and orange interchangeably; their evidentiary meanings are fixed.
Don't imply that a learner-state mutation has happened before explicit human approval.
